Degree-Preserving Network Shuffling via Edge Swaps

Source: R/shuffling.R
shuffle_network_deg.Rd

This function shuffles a directed network while preserving in-degree and out-degree. It follows a controlled randomization process by swapping edges iteratively. Similar to the curve_ball() function but more computationally demanding. This function is useful for generating increasingly randomized networks, to generate fully randomized networks, the curve_ball() function is preferred.

Usage

shuffle_network_deg(
  input_graph,
  delta = 100,
  directed = TRUE,
  weighted = TRUE,
  fix_loops = FALSE
)

Arguments

input_graph

An igraph object or a square adjacency matrix (directed, weighted or unweighted).

delta

Number of edge swaps to perform.

directed

Logical. Whether the network is directed (default: TRUE).

weighted

Logical. Whether the network is weighted (default: TRUE). When FALSE a warning is given if the matrix has values greater than 1 (a multigraph).

fix_loops

Logical. If TRUE the self-loops (the diagonal) are kept fixed during the randomization (default: FALSE, the diagonal is randomized like any other cell).

Value

A shuffled adjacency matrix preserving in-degree and out-degree.

Details

The function preserves the total in-degree and out-degree (row and column totals) of the adjacency matrix, but it does not preserve the degree of each layer of a multilayer network nor the reciprocity: reciprocal pairs A->B / B->A (e.g. mutualism, competition) are separated by the swaps.

By default the diagonal is not avoided, so the swaps can create and destroy self-loops (cannibalism in food-webs). In food-webs with 14-15 loops only 5-8 were left after about two swaps per link. A loop always falls inside its own module, so losing loops lowers the modularity of the randomized networks and makes the empirical network look more modular than it is. With fix_loops = TRUE the loops are kept fixed: they are never selected for a swap and a swap that would create a new loop is rejected.

References

Huaylla, C. A., Nacif, M. E., Coulin, C., Kuperman, M. N., & Garibaldi, L. A. (2021). Decoding information in multilayer ecological networks: The keystone species case. Ecological Modelling, 460, 109734. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2021.109734

Strona, G., Nappo, D., Boccacci, F., Fattorini, S., & San-Miguel-Ayanz, J. (2014). A fast and unbiased procedure to randomize ecological binary matrices with fixed row and column totals. Nature Communications, 5, 4114. https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms5114
